title: Browser Extensions & Privacy Add-ons Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete security checklist for browser extensions and privacy add-ons. Protect yourself from malicious extensions and configure privacy tools properly.
intro: Browser extensions can enhance your privacy but also pose security risks. This checklist helps you safely install, configure, and maintain privacy-focused extensions while avoiding common pitfalls that could compromise your security.

items.task: Only install extensions from official browser stores
items.why: Official stores have security reviews and can quickly remove malicious extensions, reducing risk of installing compromised software.
items.howTo: Use Chrome Web Store for Chrome/Edge, Firefox Add-ons for Firefox, or Safari Extensions for Safari. Never download.crx or.xpi files from unknown websites.

items.task: Verify extension developer reputation and reviews
items.why: Established developers with good track records are less likely to distribute malicious code or sell user data.
items.howTo: Check developer name, website, user reviews, and download count. Look for extensions with 100K+ users and 4+ star ratings from reputable developers.

items.task: Review all requested permissions before installing
items.why: Extensions requesting excessive permissions may be collecting unnecessary data or have broader access than needed for their function.
items.howTo: Read the permission list during installation. Question why an ad blocker needs access to your camera, or why a password manager needs microphone access.

items.task: Verify extensions receive regular security updates
items.why: Outdated extensions may contain security vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to compromise your browser or data.
items.howTo: Check the extension's 'Last updated' date in the store. Avoid extensions not updated in 6+ months unless they're mature and stable projects.

items.why: Too many extensions increase attack surface, can conflict with each other, and may slow down your browser performance.
items.howTo: Start with 3-5 core privacy extensions: uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger, and a password manager. Add others only if genuinely needed.

items.task: Configure uBlock Origin with recommended filter lists
items.why: Proper filter list configuration maximizes ad and tracker blocking while minimizing false positives that break websites.
items.howTo: Enable EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock filters, and regional lists. Consider enabling Fanboy's Annoyances for social media widgets and cookie notices.

items.task: Set up Privacy Badger for automatic tracker learning
items.why: Privacy Badger learns to block trackers automatically as you browse, providing dynamic protection against new tracking methods.
items.howTo: Install Privacy Badger and let it learn for a few weeks. Check its findings periodically and whitelist any legitimate services that get blocked.

items.task: Configure cookie and storage management extensions
items.why: Proper cookie management prevents long-term tracking while maintaining website functionality for sites you trust.
items.howTo: Use extensions like Cookie AutoDelete to automatically clear cookies when tabs close, with exceptions for trusted sites you want to stay logged into.

items.task: Set up JavaScript blocking extensions carefully
items.why: JavaScript blockers provide strong privacy protection but require careful configuration to avoid breaking essential website functionality.
items.howTo: If using NoScript or similar, start in 'learning mode' and gradually whitelist trusted domains. Consider uBlock Origin's medium mode as an alternative.

items.task: Enable HTTPS enforcement extensions or browser settings
items.why: HTTPS encryption protects your data from interception and tampering during transmission between your browser and websites.
items.howTo: Modern browsers have built-in HTTPS-only modes. Enable in browser settings or use extensions like HTTPS Everywhere for older browser versions.

items.why: Extensions can change ownership, add new permissions, or become compromised over time without user notification.
items.howTo: Review your extension list every 3 months. Remove unused extensions and check if remaining ones still have good reputations and recent updates.

items.task: Monitor for new permission requests from existing extensions
items.why: Extensions may request additional permissions in updates, potentially expanding their data access beyond original scope.
items.howTo: Pay attention to permission change notifications. Investigate why an extension needs new permissions before accepting the update.

items.task: Test for extension conflicts and performance issues
items.why: Multiple extensions performing similar functions can conflict, cause performance problems, or create security gaps.
items.howTo: Disable extensions one by one if experiencing issues. Use browser task manager to identify resource-heavy extensions. Consider a privacy-focused browser for conflict-free browsing.

items.why: Having a record of your privacy extension settings makes it easier to restore your setup after browser reinstalls or migrations.
items.howTo: Take screenshots or notes of important extension settings. Some extensions like uBlock Origin allow exporting configuration backups.

items.task: Research alternative browsers and built-in privacy features
items.why: Browser-native privacy features often provide better security and performance than extensions while reducing attack surface.
items.howTo: Test privacy-focused privacy-focused browsers like Firefox with strict settings, or Brave. Compare built-in blocking vs. extension-based protection.

pro_tips: Use browser profiles to separate different extension setups for work, personal, and high-privacy browsing sessions.
Enable automatic extension updates but monitor permission changes - set up email notifications if your browser supports them.
Test critical websites in incognito/private mode first when installing aggressive privacy extensions to identify potential conflicts.
Consider using a privacy-focused browser as your primary browser - it has built-in privacy features that reduce the need for multiple extensions.
Keep a 'clean' browser profile with minimal extensions for banking and other sensitive activities to reduce attack surface.
